x: Ray Middleton, fantastic as ever in his British vest, shakes off a bad season with a superlative display in Athens comes back and Wilf Wesch beats him.
Booking arrangements misfired so a powerful Belgrave squad spent a hilarious night in the back of the Duncanmobile, accomodation which was not quite what Hotelier W.
Wilf Wesch held off a slightly suspect Ken Easlea for a very strong win with Doug Fotheringham whipping round the hills to take the Handicap.

Wilf Wesch walked a powerful 30 Kilo Leg for Young England holding Pamich to two minutes and in the 100 Kilometres Pat Duncan pulled back six minutes on last year for a personal best 10:15:00 catching world champion Hohne, nearly ?

Obviously terrified by Wilf Wesch's rising reputation Frankfurt's two leading men thought better of even starting the race which was held over a very fast 15 lap course closed to all traffic except prams ( and to our cost,Kite strings!) Since then Carl Lawton, Wilf Wesch and Bob Coates have really developed, benefitting no doubt from hard sessions together both on the road at Wimbledon and during the summer on the track.
The faster boys obviously suffered less from Christmas although it was Doug Fotheringham who pulled out the suprise. Wilf Wesch produced the fastest time.

Great walks from Wilf Wesch, Carl Lawton and Len Duquemin with good support from Ray Middleton gave Belgrave a clear victory in this police race which, for many walkers, is the unofficial championship of the year.

A tremendous performance from Wilf Wesch who roared straight off the front of a fast field and stayed there throughout the race. Bob Coates could not hold him down the hills but pulled it back so well over the last three miles that Wilf only finished 7 seconds ahead.
Up front Carl Lawton finished fifth ahead of Wilf Wesch who was just clear of Bob Coates. This must be Carl's best ever 10 and puts him in with a chance for top honours this year.
Wilf Wesch led the boys home with Carl in close attendance . Len pulled out a big one and Ray shook off his earlier sickness to move through the field with deceptive ease.

In the Surrey at Mitcham Wilf Wesch retained the title he won last year with Carl Lawton and Ray Middleton taking the minor placings. In the Team race Belgrave packed as well as could be expected to return minimum points for probably the first time ever in this event.

They were approached by a flabby German called Wesch who reckoned he'd done a bit of walking - naturally being Belgrave men they smashed him into the ground leaving him at the furthest point from the changing rooms.

Wilf Wesch goes from strength to strength following his National 10 Mile win by dominating the 20 Kilometres, the 20 Miles, his new wife and the inter-counties 10,000 Metres not to mention numerous other victories including a world class time in the Met WC 20 Kilos.

Only Len Duquemin could hang on to Wilf Wesch and by six miles even he found it impossible as Wilf stormed through rain and wind to record a terrific 2: 37: 38 for a new record over this tough and accurately measured course.

The first four places in the Surrey County 10,000 Metres were all filled by claret and gold, or would have been if Ray Middleton had a club vest. Wilf Wesch walked very well on a rough track to lap the field.
Wilf Wesch walked his customary race from the front for his secnnd National victory over Wallwork and with the lads all backing well we looked all set.
Wilf Wesch missed this one in favour of the Inter-Counties race the next day and only an inspired performance from Pat Duncan held off Basildon as Carl Lawton cracked something horrible.

If I have to admit to supreme moments it was surely when I saw Wilf Wesch win two Individual titles backed up by others to give us R.W.A. Team Championships; and when we won the Southern Road Relay Championship.
In his first international appearance for West Germany Wilf Wesch flattened the opposition, from France, Sweden as well as his own team to record as fast 91.21 for 20 Kilometres.

This year a very popular choice was WILF WESCH for his win with RWA 20 Miles Championship -- one of the three main titles that he won. With the Cup's association with our first ever Olympic champion it will be interesting to see whether WILF can emulate the donor at Munich in 1972 -- forty years on…
We have to thank the hotel manager for this beneficial move - he is none other than our home-grown German walking champion, Wilf Wesch. We wish him many more years at the Parkway.
Both these walkers are from West Germany, Pape has beaten Wilf Wesch. Belgrave's other representative Bernard Capener did not live up to the promise he showed earlier this year.
Commonwealth 20 Mile Champion (1966) Ron Wallwork got the better of Wilf Wesch for the first time this year and Ray Middleton, despite a heavy racing programme showed a good turn of speed.
Some great performances from the boys gave Belgrave a comfortable victory over Basildon AC in the team and Wilf Wesch the coveted 8 Miles in the hour plaque.
Unfortunately this race coincided with Wilf Wesch's accounts so we were denied what might have been a fantastic race between John Knifton, Wilf and Bill Sutherland.
Over 20 Kilos Wilf Wesch proved himself the'fastest man in the West' with a 90:16 clocking but still only finished 7th. He did have the satisfaction of screwing his old rival Nemerich however.
On the second leg Wilf Wesch took over from Pat and attacked Paul Nihill's 1963 record with a ferocity which left it shattered by some two minutes.

With a superb display of speed Wilf Wesch beat 50 Minutes and Bob Dobson by just 1 second. Barry Ingarfield was disqualified and although McMullen deputised to good effect we were not up to the strength of Basildon in the team.

The way he streaked away from our own Wilf Wesch was a wonderful sight for those who appreciate fast walking at its best. For the first lap Wilf was in close attendance and with the hills to come Belgrave supporters could be foregiven for thinking that Wilf's extra strength would prove conclusive over the second lap.

Wilf Wesch was deservedly removed from the reckoning after some 2 miles had been covered. Wilf was seeking to establish a lead at the time and in the manner of a distance runner seeking greater speed his stride tends to shorten.

On January 16th in Battersea Park Wilf Wesch completed 10 Miles in 70:55 2 minutes ahead of Phil Embleton. In the same race Barry Ingarfield recorded a personal best 78:16 with Dave McMullen finishing 6th in 82:58.

As expected Wilf Wesch had little trouble retaining the Murphy Shield. His 74:26 done without exertion shows just how far he has come since last year when he won the title, with all stops out, only 30 seconds faster.

Belgrave suffered when Wilf Wesch was pulled while disputing the lead with Shuan Lightman but this gave Carl Lawton the chance to excell as he pulled back Lightman from over a minute to just 30 seconds at the finish.
Tragedy struck in the Surrey when Wilf Wesch, last year's winner missed his train leaving Ray Hall to close the Belgrave four in behind Surrey Walking Club.

A specially arranged sharpener before the National '10' gave Tommy Cook the opportunity to romp away with the prize closely pursued by Johnny Morris and John Keown. Wilf Wesch was the fastest man of the day although Ray Middleton, John Moullin and Andy LeHeron were also impressive.
Wilf Wesch, the reigning champion, was concentrating on staying safely in the race and avoiding any possible trouble he finished a comfortable fifth.

Wilf Wesch thrashed his german team mates for an impressive third place while Ray Middleton, Barry Ingarfield and John Moullin made up for the absence of some of our other stars to ensure that Belgrave won the team event.
In the Surrey 10,000 Metres Wilf Wesch had no trouble retaining his title with Carl Lawton also showing strong form.
Walking in the West Germany Indoor 10,000 Metre Championships Wilf Wesch recorded an impressive victory for his German Club Eintracht Frankfurt.
In trying conditions Wilf Wesch dominated this race from start to finish and never looked even tired by the effort of recording an excellent 2:39:07.
Wilf Wesch is obviously as fit as ever, so is Carl Lawton. Alan Callow is struggling to right a back injury but Ray Middleton is on the rising fitness trail once more.

In the 20 Kilos, won by Phil Embleton Wilf Wesch finished 8th in 97.10. The other side of town saw Alan Callow and Barry Ingarfield covering 12,323 Metres and 12,276 metres to finish 13th and 15th respectively in the Highgate 1 Hour Track Walks.
Wilf Wesch was in blazing form although he had Carl Lawton on his heels for most of the race. Len Duquemin and Ray Middleton also showed that they are still forces to be reckoned with.
Wilf Wesch cannot be forgotten. He of course represented West Germany at Munich in the Olympic Games, finishing 16th in 1hr.35min. 20.6 secs.

The ubiquitous WILF WESCH is now Manager of the Sport Hotel Adidas at 8522 Herzogenaurach, Beethovenstrasse 6, West Germany. The luxurious hotel is equipped with facilities for a real sportsman's holiday.

The Committee proposed George Chantler and Jim Heathfield as Vice-Presidents and from the floor our 1972 Olympic trio of Cliff Brooks, Wilf Wesch and John Bicourt together with Bill Merryman were also put forward.
